If the chains have all converged to the posterior,
$W$ and $\hat V$ both estimate the posterior variance,
and $\hR$ is close to 1.
If the chains are still exploring different regions,
the chain means differ,
$B$ is large,
and $\hR$ exceeds 1.
This statistic is also called the **Gelman--Rubin statistic**;
it formally assesses whether several chains have converged
[@dobson4e, Chapter 13, p. 306].
Software reports $\hR$ as `psrf` or `Rhat`;
`coda::gelman.diag()` also applies a small-sample correction,
so its value differs slightly from @def-psrf's.
A value of $\hR$ near 1 does not prove convergence:
chains that are all stuck in the same wrong region also agree.
